project.title: Collective Decisions in Shared Spaces
project.description: My MSc thesis proposal: a shared room where people signal discreetly how it affects them, and a display shows the group's rule and who is still uncomfortable, never who asked.
project.introText: Offices, libraries, study rooms and waiting rooms already decide whose comfort counts, but the decision stays hidden, and their technology is designed around a default occupant. My MSc thesis asks how a shared adaptive space can make its decisions visible and open to challenge, so that people who usually stay silent have a say without being singled out.
project.middleText: Asking for a change exposes a need in front of others, so those furthest from the default, such as women, trans and non-binary people, and neurodivergent and disabled people, often stay silent; even indoor-climate standards rest on the metabolic rate of an average adult man. In the concept, people signal discreetly how the space affects them, the room combines the signals with a rule the group can change, such as majority or most affected first, and a shared display shows the spread of needs, the rule and who is still uncomfortable, never who asked. The thesis follows research through design in four phases: interviews and observations, two co-design workshops, an iterative prototype, and a within-group study in one shared university room, with groups doing real work.
project.context: MSc thesis proposal, “Visualizing Collective Decision-Making in Shared Adaptive Spaces: Agency, fairness and inclusion in Human-Building Interaction”, MSc Information Studies (Human-Computer Interaction), University of Amsterdam

summary.brief: Asking a shared room for a change exposes a need in front of others.
summary.role: Solo: research, design and study (MSc thesis).
summary.method: Research through design in four phases: interviews with people who share and manage university rooms, two co-design workshops, an iterative prototype, and a within-group study of agency, perceived fairness and comfort.

facts: participants planned for the study, in 5 or 6 groups of 4 to 6
project.shows: Research through design on a question of fairness: who gets a say in a shared room, and how to give it without exposing anyone.
